THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7806  CRL.P No. 101433 of 2024  ORDER Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned HCGP for the respondent - State.
2. The petitioners - accused Nos.1, 2 and 4 have been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 408, 409, 420, 465, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Trial Court.

4. The summary of the charge sheet is that accused No.1 was Ex-Gram Panchayat Member of Todalabagi Gram Panchayat, accused No.2 was in-charge Panchayat Development Officer and accused No.4 was Chairman of Todalabagi Gram Panchayat.

They misappropriated a sum of Rs.3,42,375/- and caused loss to the State Exchequer in respect of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme by creating false NMR account through the bank account of the said Gram Panchayat.

entities.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, the first informant lodged the complaint.

5. The learned Magistrate after receipt of the charge sheet, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons and framed charges against accused Nos.1 to 4.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7806

During the course of evidence, i.e., while examining PW1, the prosecution produced permission letter issued by the Chief Executive Officer, Zilla Panchayat, Bagalakote to prosecute the accused persons alongwith an application under Sections 242(2) and (3) of Cr.P.C.
and same was opposed by accused Nos.1 to 4.
In-turn, the Trial Court proceeded to allow the application and permitted the prosecution to produce the said document.
Aggrieved by the said order, the petitioners - accused Nos.1, 2 and 4 have preferred this petition to quash the said order.
6. It is contended that during the course of evidence, the aforesaid document has been produced, in fact proposed document was not a part of the charge sheet.
They could have filed said document under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C.
The proposed document ought to have been submitted alongwith charge sheet, but during the course of trial, the aforesaid document furnished with antedate which is not permissible under law.

7. Learned HCGP for respondent - State contended that the Trial Court based on material fact and in compliance with Section 242(2) of Cr.P.C. has rightly allowed the appeal NC: 2024:KHC-D:7806 and permitted the prosecution to rely on the said documents.
Hence, prayed to reject the petition.

sentences.text: Perused the petition, documents, impugned order and contentions taken by both the parties.

It appears that the prosecution submitted a document issued by Chief Executive Officer, Zilla Panchayat, wherein the Chief Executive Officer, Zilla Panchayat permitted the first informant to lodge complaint against the accused persons.
From the perusal of the charge sheet, the Investigating Officer has not collected these documents.

Therefore, the prosecution relied upon this document during the course of trial and made effort to mark said document through first informant i.e., PW1.
9.
At this juncture, the counsel for accused objected the same.

Hence, it is just and necessary to analyze Sections 242(2) and (3) of Cr.P.C. which reads as under:
"242(2) The Magistrate may, on the application of the prosecution, issue a summons to any of its witnesses directing him to attend or to produce any document or other thing.
(3) On the date so fixed, the Magistrate shall proceed to take all such evidence as may be produced in support of the prosecution:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7806 Provided that the Magistrate may permit the cross-examination of any witness to be deferred until any other witness or witnesses have been examined or recall any witness for further cross- examination."
10.

From the perusal of the above said provision of law, it clearly establishes that the Trial Court may, on the application of the prosecution, issue summons to any of its witness, directing him to attend or to produce any document for just decision of the case.
11. It is settled law that, mere production of any relevant document is a ministerial act, but appreciation of such document is a judicial act.
Mere production of any disputed document is not dispensed with any proof.
Unless the proposed document is marked in evidence, the accused cannot object it.
12. The Trial Court has rightly allowed the application in terms of Section 242(2) of Cr.P.C.
It is pertinent to note that, if the proposed document is not marked in evidence, more harm would be caused to the prosecution than the accused persons.
Hence, there is no merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners.
Accordingly, the criminal petition is NC: 2024:KHC-D:7806 dismissed.

The order dated 03.05.2024 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Jamkhandi is confirmed.
Send the copy of this order to the Trial Court forthwith.

Sd/-
